title: StraGCN: GPU-Accelerated Strassen's Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication for Graph Convolutional Network Training
problem: Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) suffer from high computational cost during training due to inefficient Sparse-Dense Matrix Multiplication (SpMM), limiting scalability and throughput.
motivation: GCNs are fundamental for deep learning on graph-structured data, but training bottleneck is the SpMM operation which occurs repeatedly. Existing GPU implementations using multi-stream CUDA model have poor data locality and redundant computations. Strassen's algorithm offers computational asymptotic improvement, but practical GPU implementation for GCN SpMM is unexplored.
method: GPU-accelerated SpMM using Strassen's algorithm with three key optimizations: (1) horizontal fusion model for kernels improving shared memory locality, (2) intermediate result reuse exploiting adjacency matrix immutability, (3) two-stage matrix partitioning to balance load irregularities from sparse structure.
key_novelty: First practical GPU-accelerated Strassen SpMM implementation specifically optimized for GCN training, combining algorithmic improvements with GPU architecture-aware optimizations.
contributions: Horizontal kernel fusion model as alternative to multi-stream CUDA for improved data locality
Intermediate result reuse strategy leveraging GCN adjacency matrix immutability
Two-stage matrix partitioning addressing load imbalance from irregular sparsity patterns
Comprehensive evaluation on 15 benchmark datasets showing 2.1-3.3x speedup over GNNA, PyG, DGL
limitations: Abstract-only; specific details on memory requirements, scalability limits, and applicability to other sparse matrix operations not provided.
primary_theme: Specialized GPU kernels for graph neural networks
